prompt: Three engineers must choose a startup direction. Option A is an AI meal planner copied from funding news, with no observed user problem. Option B is a radiology-triage idea one founder heard at a conference; they have no hospital access, and a wrong output could harm a patient. Option C is invoice reconciliation that two founders handled at a logistics company; eleven controllers still do it weekly, and four will pay for a pilot. The CEO proposes spending $30,000 on ads and letting clicks choose the company. Give a two-week opportunity decision plan and the ordered next handoff.
criteria: Chooses invoice reconciliation as the provisional direction because of direct founder knowledge, access, urgent repeated work, and paid-pilot commitments; rejects fashion and clicks as demand evidence.
Gives every candidate a dated deepen, stop, or discard disposition and falsifier while recording user problem, founder access, urgency, timing or why-now, wedge, expansion path, and disqualifiers.
Treats radiology as high-harm and access-constrained, refusing unsafe crude use and requiring reversible staged evidence or specialist access before reconsideration.
Uses the order choosing-startup-opportunities then learning-from-users, allowing growth before validation only to recruit the defined sample or seed its narrow learning beachhead.

Hands learning-from-users an explicit hypothesis, sample, evidence threshold, and review date, and releases growth ownership only after real use, payment, or a predefined equally discriminating commitment.
scoring: Award one point per criterion only when operationalized. Compare five blind controls with five current-skill guided responses.
